title: Lyon §4.4 feature lines + boundary alignment in motorcycle graph
description:
Lyon §4.4: feature edges (sharp creases) and boundary edges should be represented as arcs in the layout. Implementation: trace motorcycles ALONG feature/boundary curves at α=0 (no deviation allowed). These traces become layout arcs by construction.

Without this, our rocker-arm output doesn't follow the bolt-hole rims cleanly — the bolt holes are mesh boundaries that should be layout arcs but currently aren't traced as such.

Implementation:
1. Detect feature edges via dihedral angle threshold + boundary edges (already done in SemanticPatchDecomposer).
2. In MotorcycleGraph.trace, BEFORE singularity-launched motorcycles, launch boundary-following motorcycles along each boundary loop and feature curve.
3. Use α=0 for these, ensuring they don't deviate.
4. Other motorcycles treat them as walls (Eppstein behavior — they always stop at boundary traces).

Matters for: meshes with bolt holes, sharp creases, open boundaries (rocker-arm, brackets, mechanical parts).
definition-of-done: Rocker-arm: bolt-hole rims are explicitly layout arcs (visible in the overlay as patch boundaries hugging the holes). Hand-30k mesh has no boundaries so no behavior change there.
testing-plan: Toy: cube with one face removed (so 4 boundary edges) → boundary loop emerges as 4 connected layout arcs. Rocker-arm: visually inspect overlay around bolt holes.
